text:
Alex: Heads up — PR #12045 touches the KV cache header and auth glue. Need runtime + security eyes for a quick greenlight. Targeting merge in tomorrow's 10:00–11:00 UTC merge window. PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/12045

Sam: @Alex can you paste the perf run output? I want to make sure the new eviction header doesn't regress tail latency.

Alex: pasted the perf gist: `https://gist.github.com/ax/perf-run-12045` — 95th p99 looks +3ms on a synthetic microbench for long sequences, but end-to-end infra tests are clean.

Jordan: re infra, the change touches request routing headers we use in node placement. Quick note: if this lands before we roll the new eviction policy, we might need a short hotfix. Can we gate with a canary?

Alex: Yes — plan is canary on 10% of traffic for 30m, auto-rollback on error rate spike. I'll add canary rule to the rollout config in the PR.

Ryan: @Alex thanks. Security question: the auth glue touches token propagation. I need either a short checklist in the PR description (how tokens are forwarded, KMS use, any new scopes) or a small ADR link. I can't approve without that.

Alex: added a checklist to the PR description: 1) tokens proxied, not re-signed; 2) no new key material stored; 3) KMS used for rotation; 4) no user PII added to headers. Linked ADR: https://docs.company/adr/eviction-token-handling

CI-bot: build passed — all unit & integration checks green. perf/regression-check: queued (will post results).

Sam: If perf regression-check is green, I can approve after a quick smoke on canary. Call out any long-seq traffic we should include.

Maya: quick ops check — let's schedule the canary at 10:15 UTC instead of 10:00 so SRE can monitor from shift start.

Alex: updated merge window to 10:15–11:15 UTC and added canary policy (10% for 30m). CI perf-check finished: no regression beyond noise. Link in PR.

Ryan: ok reviewed checklist + ADR. Leaving a final security approval note in PR. Approve once canary is set.

Sam: ran a short canary smoke locally, looks fine. Approving pending no canary alarms.

Maya: SRE will watch 10:15–10:45 UTC, will ping in #eng-sre if anything odd.

Alex: thanks everyone — will merge at ~10:20 UTC if canary looks healthy. :rocket:
